candidates.exact_span: The percent solids of sewage sludge that contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 90% based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets an enforceable numeric solids limit; different readings of the measurement basis ('moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials') or whether sludge qualifies as containing unstabilized primary solids could change which limit applies or whether a reported solids measurement exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines whether the 90% solids limit is applicable at all; interpretation of whether reported sludge contains qualifying unstabilized solids could change whether a numeric limit comparison is required.

candidates.exact_span: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) Test - Once/Permit Life, performed within one year from the effective date of the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Declares a monitoring obligation with permit-life frequency and a one-year startup window; interpretation of permit effective date or whether the permit-life test was satisfied could change required monitoring for FY2025 and whether absent TCLP results reflect a missing-evidence case versus a resolved no-requirement state.
Establishes an annual PCB monitoring requirement; whether this requirement is treated as applicable for a given facility or period could change evaluated monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: All other pollutants shall be monitored at the frequency shown below:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scopes which pollutants follow the tiered sludge-amount frequency table rather than the explicit TCLP/PCB schedules; interpretation of what counts as an 'other pollutant' could change which monitoring frequencies apply.

candidates.exact_span:
0 ≤ Sludge < 290                                       Once/Year
    290 ≤ Sludge < 1,500                                   Once/Quarter
    1,500 ≤ Sludge < 15,000                                Once/Two Months
    15,000 ≤ Sludge                                        Once/Month
candidates.computation_change_reason: Tiered monitoring frequencies depend on annual sludge amount; different classification of a facility's metric-ton total could change how often monitoring was required and whether missing results represent inadequate evidence versus an unresolved applicability case.

candidates.exact_span: *Either the amount of bulk sewage sludge applied to the land or the amount of sewage sludge received by a person who prepares sewage sludge that is sold or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land (dry weight basis).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines which sludge quantity metric sets monitoring frequency; choosing bulk-applied versus bagged/container-prepared dry-weight totals could change the applicable tier and therefore FY2025 monitoring expectations and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Representative samples of sewage sludge shall be collected and analyzed in accordance with the methods referenced in 40 CFR 503.8(b).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the required sampling and analytical methods for reported measurements; interpretation of whether available results were collected and analyzed under these methods could change whether a numeric limit comparison is valid or whether monitoring evidence satisfies the stated obligation.

candidates.exact_span: For those permittees meeting Class A or B pathogen reduction requirements and that meet the cumulative loading rates in Table 2 below, or the Class B pathogen reduction requirements and contain
candidates.computation_change_reason: Gates Section II requirements on pathogen class and Table 2/Table 3 conditions; interpretation of whether a permittee satisfies these prerequisites could change which pollutant limits, monitoring rules, and missing-evidence cases are in scope for FY2025.
